definitions.explanation: Naturally black hair, often with connotations of beauty and elegance in Japanese culture.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{美|うつく}しい{黒髪|くろかみ}をしている。
{最近|さいきん}は{黒髪|くろかみ}ストレートが{人気|にんき}だ。
examples.english: Straight black hair has been popular recently.

examples.japanese: {長|なが}い{黒髪|くろかみ}を{風|かぜ}になびかせて{歩|ある}く{姿|すがた}が{印象的|いんしょうてき}だった。
examples.english: The sight of her walking with her long black hair flowing in the wind was striking.

notes:
Composed of {黒|くろ} (black) + {髪|かみ} (hair). In Japanese culture, {黒髪|くろかみ} has traditionally been associated with beauty and elegance, especially in literature and poetry. The word carries more aesthetic weight than simply saying {黒|くろ}い{髪|かみ} (black-colored hair).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {美|うつく}しい{黒髪|くろかみ}: beautiful black hair
- {長|なが}い{黒髪|くろかみ}: long black hair
- {黒髪|くろかみ}ストレート: straight black hair
- {艶|つや}やかな{黒髪|くろかみ}: glossy black hair
- {黒髪|くろかみ}に{戻|もど}す: to go back to black hair (after dyeing)

CULTURAL NOTE:
In traditional Japanese aesthetics, long, straight {黒髪|くろかみ} was considered the ideal of feminine beauty. This image persists in modern culture, though hair dyeing is now very common.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {白髪|しらが}: gray hair, white hair — often a sign of aging
- {金髪|きんぱつ}: blond hair — natural or dyed
- {茶髪|ちゃぱつ}: brown-dyed hair — common among Japanese youth
